_comment: Where Lafayette Square's data wells are. Shape: cartograph/sources.js.
_ls_is_reference_consumer_one: ⛔ LS is the mould the kit was cast around, not the subject. This file exists so bake-content.js#loadParcels could stop hardcoding LS's filenames for every town in the world — it changes nothing about LS's own pour.

parcels.attribution: City of St. Louis Assessor — Assessor_Public_Parcels
parcels._note: St. Louis City is an INDEPENDENT CITY — its assessor holds only City parcels. The historical acquisition is scripts/03-fetch-stl-parcels.py, which also folds AprComImprove into appraised_value, LastYearBuilt into year_built and NbrOfBldgsCom into num_buildings, and reads LocalHistDist/CertLocalHistDist. cartograph/fetch-parcels.mjs maps one column per field, so re-fetching through the button would lose those second operands. ⛔ The existing raw/stl_parcels.json is the Python script's output and must NOT be re-fetched through the button until the field map grows a fallback-column form. Declared here so the FILENAME hardcode could die; the endpoint is recorded, not yet exercised on this town.

_landUseCodes_why: null = self-describing/not needed here. LS sits entirely in St. Louis City, whose AsrLandUse1 codes are read by the stl-assessor-numeric ranges in bake-content.js#classifyUse; the county-land-use-codes.csv decode table is a COUNTY artifact and LS has no county parcels. (LS also has no content/ dir at all — INTAKE-CATALOGUE §3.5 T3 — so bake-content refuses it without --force.)
